title: Ship evalctl v0.1 artifact harness
description:
evalctl v0.1 needs to prove a local-first agent evaluation path end to end: a code-review suite runs synchronously, an agent-under-test is invoked as a local runner, deterministic scorers grade the resulting workspace and response artifacts, and a self-contained run directory can regenerate the report without the original suite or runner environment.

The first release is intentionally narrow. It must not build hosted services, an inference proxy, async queueing, execution replay, mutating suite/case/scorer add commands, command scorers, or model-route provenance. The differentiated product is the workspace-scoring artifact, not prompt regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl init`, `validate`, `run`, `status`, `report`, `capabilities`, `schema`, and `robot-docs guide` support the synchronous code-review path.
- Every implemented JSON output uses the universal envelope and published exit-code/error-code contract.
- Runs produce portable run directories with suite snapshots, per-case inputs, runner artifacts, workspace manifests, derived scores, and reports.
- Deterministic built-in scorers include `workspace-diff` and can recompute reports from copied run artifacts.
- The v0.1 artifact replay success test passes from a copied run directory without invoking the original runner.
notes:
CLOSED:
- v0.1 synchronous code-review path implemented through init, validate, run, status, report, capabilities, schema, and robot-docs guide.
- Universal JSON envelope, code registry, exit-code dictionary, runner safety warnings, deterministic scorers, workspace manifests, portable run directories, and artifact replay are covered.
- Child issues evalctl-97b.1 through evalctl-97b.12 are closed against implementation commit 449ded0.
- Verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v; python3 -m py_compile evalctl/cli.py evalctl/__main__.py evalctl/__init__.py tests/test_evalctl.py.
close_reason: evalctl v0.1 artifact harness complete: contract, suite scaffold, runner execution, manifests, scorers, run/status/report, artifact replay, docs, and conformance tests — commit 449ded0

title: Implement CLI contract skeleton
description: The CLI needs a machine-first contract before behavior is implemented so agents can discover verbs, flags, schemas, exit codes, and follow-up commands without scraping human help text.
design:
Implement `capabilities --json`, `schema <verb> --json`, core `--help`, the universal JSON envelope, the code registry, the exit-code dictionary, and the `integrations` discoverability block for planned `spoolctl` and `inferctl` support.

Every `--json` result, including `capabilities` and `schema`, should be wrapped as `{ok, tool_version, data, meta, warnings, commands, errors}`. `meta.data_hash` is computed from canonicalized `data` with volatile fields excluded. Human rendering is a projection chosen only when stdout is a TTY and no explicit machine format was requested.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl capabilities --json` returns the universal envelope with `contract_version`, implemented verbs, flags, env vars, schemas, exit-code dictionary, code registry references, and integrations where `spoolctl` and `inferctl` are `available:false` and `planned:true`.
- `evalctl schema <verb> --json` returns the envelope for each implemented verb.
- All implemented verbs accept `--json`; `report --format json` is accepted as an alias for `report --json`.
- JSON stdout is parseable and contains no ANSI escapes; diagnostics and mirrored errors go to stderr.
- Golden tests pin `capabilities --json` and implemented verb schemas with volatile metadata excluded.

title: Implement artifact replay success test
description: The v0.1 ship gate is artifact replay: a second agent must be able to copy a run directory, regenerate the report, and recompute deterministic scorers without the original suite path or runner environment.
design: Build an acceptance harness that runs the code-review suite, copies the resulting run directory to a clean location without an `evals/` root and without invoking the runner, runs `evalctl report --run-dir <copied> --format json`, recomputes scorers from persisted artifacts, and compares the regenerated `data.report_hash` against the original.
acceptance_criteria:
- The harness exercises at least one passing and one failing case.
- Recomputed scorers use `suite-snapshot/`, `input.json`, `output.*`, `runner.json`, `workspace-before.json`, and `workspace-after.json`; original `score.json` is not trusted.
- The regenerated normalized report hash equals the original when artifacts are unchanged.
- No runner command is invoked during artifact replay.
- A changed artifact causes a report-hash mismatch or explicit validation error.
close_reason: Added artifact replay test that copies a run directory, removes the original evals root, recomputes scores from artifacts, and verifies report_hash stability — commit 449ded0

Document runner safety, output format rules, exit codes, artifact replay, relative run-directory paths, and the deferred status of async queueing, execution replay, command scorers, `compare`, and mutating add verbs.

title: Pin determinism and conformance tests
description: The v0.1 release needs regression tests that enforce the agent-first CLI contract, deterministic surfaces, and make-cli conformance checklist.
design: Add golden tests for `capabilities --json`, `schema <verb> --json`, and normalized `report --format json` data. Exclude volatile domains such as request id, wall-clock timestamps, elapsed time, run id, created timestamp, runner duration, and future job or route snapshots. title: Define suite and case schemas
description: evalctl needs explicit suite and case formats so hand-edited eval files can be validated before any runner executes local code.
design: Define a suite directory containing `suite.json`, `cases.jsonl`, and fixtures. Define case objects with stable `id`, `task`, `workspace`, optional `diff`, and `expect` fields for built-in scorers. Resolve paths relative to the suite directory. Treat `diff` as review material exposed through `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE`; do not apply it to the workspace in v0.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- `validate [<suite>] --json` reports malformed suite JSON, malformed case JSONL, missing fixture paths, invalid scorer refs, duplicate case ids, and invalid runner configuration using registered error codes.
- Case paths are resolved relative to the suite directory and recorded in diagnostics without absolute paths in portable artifacts.
- The default code-review sample suite contains at least one passing and one failing case.
- A case `diff` is exposed to the runner but not applied to the workspace unless a future explicit option is added.

title: Scaffold sample code-review suite
description: New users and agents need a concrete code-review suite that demonstrates the intended v0.1 path without requiring mutating suite/case/scorer add commands.
design: Implement `evalctl init` to scaffold an `evals/` tree with a `code-review` suite, `suite.json`, `cases.jsonl`, fixtures, and sample expectations for text, exit code, file presence, and workspace-diff behavior. Keep generated files hand-editable and deterministic.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl init` creates a complete sample suite without requiring network access or a hosted service.
- Re-running `init` on an existing eval tree refuses to overwrite by default and suggests the safe command or manual path to proceed.
- The scaffolded suite validates cleanly immediately after creation.
- The scaffolded code-review suite can produce one green and one red case once run with an appropriate local runner command.
close_reason: Added evalctl init scaffold for the code-review suite with sample cases, fixtures, runner config, and safe overwrite behavior — commit 449ded0

title: Implement runner execution contract
description: The runner is the agent-under-test invocation, and v0.1 must execute it honestly as arbitrary local code while bounding reproducibility and artifact leakage.
design:
Support `runner.argv` with `shell:false` as the default and `runner.command` with `shell:true` as an explicit escape hatch. Exactly one form is valid for the selected mode. Default `cwd` to the per-case workspace. Inherit only `env_allowlist` variables and always inject `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE`, `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`, `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, `EVALCTL_TASK_FILE`, and `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE` when present.

Close stdin by default, with `runner.stdin:"task"` to pipe task text. Apply `timeout_seconds`, kill the process group on timeout, capture stdout/stderr/output up to `max_output_bytes`, and apply `redact_env_values` and `redact_patterns` before writing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- `shell:false` executes argv without implicit shell joining; `$EVALCTL_*` substitution is performed only by evalctl.
- `shell:true` executes the explicit command through `sh -c` and is documented as the less-safe escape hatch.
- Runner spawn failures and timeouts mark the case `error`; ordinary nonzero process exits are captured and scored rather than treated as tool errors.
- Every `run` emits `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` in the JSON envelope and prints the warning to stderr when appropriate unless the suite explicitly acknowledges it.
- Captured stdout, stderr, and output are truncated and redacted before persistence, with booleans recording whether truncation or redaction occurred.
close_reason: Implemented runner argv/shell validation, env injection, timeout/capture/redaction handling, and unsandboxed-runner warning support — commit 449ded0

title: Capture workspace manifests
description: The core differentiator is scoring the resulting workspace, so evalctl must capture structured before/after filesystem evidence rather than relying on textual diffs.
design: Walk the per-case workspace before and after runner execution to produce `workspace-before.json` and `workspace-after.json`. Derive `workspace-diff.json` from those manifests. Include untracked and ignored files. Represent files, directories, symlinks, and other special file types. Use POSIX-style relative UTF-8 paths with no `.` or `..` segments and no absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Full manifests contain entries with `path`, `kind`, and file hashes where applicable.
- Directories are represented by presence; binary files are represented by sha256; symlinks are not followed and store target information.
- Unreadable or unsupported non-UTF-8 paths emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` and do not silently corrupt the manifest.
- `workspace-diff.json` identifies added, modified, and deleted paths from the two structured manifests.
- Textual `workspace.diff` is best-effort and never parsed by scorers.
close_reason: Implemented before/after workspace manifests, structured diff manifests, path normalization, symlink/special-file handling, and text diff projection — commit 449ded0

title: Implement deterministic built-in scorers
description: v0.1 must grade runs with deterministic local scorers that are credible without an LLM judge and can be recomputed from persisted artifacts.
design: Implement built-in scorers for `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json-schema`, `numeric-threshold`, `file-exists`, `exit-code`, and `workspace-diff`. Each scorer emits `{ok, score, label, findings}` and respects whether it is required or advisory. Built-in scorers consume persisted, redacted outputs and structured workspace manifests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each scorer has unit tests for pass, fail, and malformed-input behavior.
- `workspace-diff` matches `expect.files_changed` and `expect.files_forbidden` using glob semantics against `changed_paths[].path`.
- `exit-code` compares expected exit code against `runner.json` and does not conflate failed expectations with tool errors.
- Required scorer failures produce case status `fail`; scorer crashes or invalid scorer inputs produce case status `error`.
- Score output is stable and can be serialized into each case `score.json`.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic built-in scorers for text, regex, exact, JSON parse, numeric threshold, file existence, exit code, and workspace diff — commit 449ded0

title: Implement synchronous run orchestration
description: v0.1 needs one complete synchronous execution path that can run a suite, invoke runners, score cases, and continue through partial failures without depending on async infrastructure.
design:
Implement `evalctl run <suite> [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--run-id <id>] [--fail-on-fail] [--json]`. Create a reservation for the run id, materialize a fresh workspace per case, execute cases with bounded concurrency, write artifacts, derive scores, update `manifest.json` atomically, and continue after case-level errors with `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.

Default `--jobs` to `min(CPU_count, 4)`. Sort iteration before serialization so JSON is deterministic regardless of completion order. Use `<UTC-timestamp>-<suite-name>` for default run ids. Reusing a completed matching run id returns the existing run; live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; semantic clashes return `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run` produces a complete run directory under `evals/runs/` with a suite snapshot and per-case artifacts.
- Case errors do not abort the whole run; the run remains reportable and emits `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.
- Eval failures exit 0 by default and set `data.run.ok:false`; `--fail-on-fail` exits 6 when any case is not `pass`.
- A live reservation returns exit 4 with `E_RUN_BUSY` and a retry recommendation; a completed mismatched run id returns exit 5 with `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
- JSON output includes paste-ready follow-up commands only for implemented verbs.
close_reason: Implemented synchronous run orchestration with per-case workspaces, run directories, scoring, partial-run warnings, run-id reuse, and fail-on-fail exit behavior — commit 449ded0

title: Build portable run directory model
description: The run directory is the v0.1 source of truth, so it must carry everything needed to inspect, report, and re-score a completed run without relying on shell history or the original suite location.
design: Write `manifest.json`, `suite-snapshot/`, and per-case `input.json`, `task.txt`, `runner.json`, stdout/stderr captures, `output.*`, before/after workspace manifests, derived `workspace-diff.json`, best-effort `workspace.diff`, and `score.json`. Keep every path recorded inside the run directory relative to the run-directory root. Treat `report.md` as a convenience copy; regenerate authoritative reports from manifest and artifacts.

- No artifact path inside `manifest.json`, score files, or report payloads is absolute.
- `suite-snapshot/` is sufficient for `status` and `report` to interpret scorer configuration from a copied run directory.
- `created_ts` and run ids are treated as volatile metadata and excluded from canonical report hashes.
- `score.json` is persisted for inspection but is not trusted as input during artifact replay.
- The run directory layout is documented by `robot-docs guide`.
close_reason: Implemented portable run directory layout with manifest, suite snapshot, per-case artifacts, relative manifest paths, and replay-safe score recomputation — commit 449ded0

title: Implement status and report commands
description: Agents need diagnose and triage commands that summarize run state, rank failures deterministically, and point to the exact artifacts needed for inspection.
design:
Implement `status <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--json]` and `report <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--format markdown|json] [--json]`. Resolve run ids under `evals/runs/`; accept copied standalone run directories through `--run-dir`. Rank report failures as `error` before `fail`, then by ascending aggregate numeric score, then case id.

`status` should include per-case state and a `recommended_action`. `report` should include aggregate scores, ranked failures, relative artifact links, and `data.report_hash` over the normalized report projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `status` works for both local run ids and copied run directories.
- `report --format json` and `report --json` both return the universal envelope.
- Markdown reports are deterministic apart from explicitly volatile metadata.
- Ranked failures are ordered by error/fail class, aggregate score, and case id.
- `commands[]` contains only implemented follow-up commands such as regenerating a JSON report.
close_reason: Implemented status and report commands for run ids and copied run directories with ranked failures, report_hash, markdown, and JSON envelopes — commit 449ded0

title: Evalctl v0.1.1 Contract Hardening
description: The v0.1 CLI advertises a stronger execution and artifact contract than it currently implements. The patch release must make the advertised contract true without changing the universal JSON envelope shape or starting v0.2 feature work.

- Every child issue acceptance check is complete.
- `python -m unittest` and `python -m compileall evalctl tests` pass in CI across supported Python versions.
- Golden data hashes are re-pinned where the contract intentionally changes.
- `contract_version` remains 1.
- CHANGELOG and README describe the corrected v0.1.1 posture.

title: Pin runner error surfaces
description: Runner timeouts and spawn failures are currently registered but not emitted by the run path. The contract needs to distinguish case-level runner facts from command-level envelope failures so agents can interpret exits, warnings, and artifacts consistently.
design:
Record per-case runner timeout or spawn failure as `status:"error"` in `manifest.cases[].status` and `score.json.status`, with `runner.json.error_code` set to `E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT`, `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, or `null`. Do not put per-case runner failures into envelope `errors[]`. Default `run` exits 0 when a reportable run contains errored cases; `--fail-on-fail` exits 6 when any case is not `pass`; exit 3 remains reserved for conditions that prevent a coherent run/report from being produced.

Add a `surface` discriminator to each `CODE_REGISTRY` entry. Codes whose appearance predicts an envelope error use `surface:"envelope"`; per-case runner reason codes use `surface:"runner_json"`. Surface this through `capabilities.error_codes` and explain the distinction in robot docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- `runner.json` includes `error_code` for every case, with timeout and spawn failure cases populated.
- Case-level timeout/spawn failure produces `W_PARTIAL_RUN`, a generated manifest/report, no envelope `errors[]`, exit 0 by default, and exit 6 under `--fail-on-fail`.
- Command-level failures that prevent a coherent report still produce exit 3 and envelope `errors[]`.
- `capabilities.error_codes` includes the new `surface` discriminator.
- Robot docs explain that `runner_json` reason codes do not predict the process exit.
- The capabilities golden hash is re-pinned.
notes:
COMPLETED:

- Added per-case runner.json.error_code for timeout/spawn failure cases.
- Updated robot docs to explain runner_json reason codes and run exit behavior.
- Added CLI regression tests for timeout and spawn failure reportability.
- Verified with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Make JSON artifact writes atomic
description: Run-directory JSON artifacts are written directly. A crash or interrupted write can leave `manifest.json` or other source-of-truth artifacts truncated at the final path.
design:
Refactor `write_json` so it writes JSON text to a temporary file in the same directory and then atomically replaces the destination with `os.replace`. Apply this uniformly to manifest, runner, score, and workspace-manifest JSON writes. This guarantees atomic visibility, not full crash-durable persistence; do not add `fsync` in v0.1.1.

Expose a small test seam around the low-level temp-write step so a unit test can force failure after temp creation and before replacement without brittle monkeypatching of `os`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Normal runs produce the same deterministic artifacts as before.
- A unit test can force an interrupted write between temp-write and replace.
- When the forced failure occurs, the previous final JSON file remains intact or absent; it is never truncated.
- The code and docs describe the guarantee as atomic visibility, not crash durability.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Replaced direct JSON writes with same-directory temp file plus os.replace atomic visibility.
- Added an injectable _atomic_write writer seam for failure tests.
- Documented atomic visibility vs crash durability in robot docs.
- Added a unit test proving temp-write failure preserves an existing final JSON file and does not create an absent final file.
- Verified with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Implement bounded jobs concurrency
description: `--jobs` is currently recorded in the manifest but cases still execute sequentially. The CLI needs real bounded parallelism while preserving deterministic evalctl-owned outputs.
design:
Parse `--jobs` as a positive integer, defaulting to `min(os.cpu_count() or 1, 4)`, and reject values below 1 with `E_CASE_INVALID`. Run `run_case` calls through `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=jobs)`. Collect `(entry, warnings)` results by case id, then rebuild `manifest.cases` and aggregated warnings in sorted case-id order.

If a runner timeout or nonzero outcome is handled inside `run_case`, keep it reportable per the runner-error contract. If a future raises unexpectedly, catch it in the orchestrator and convert it to a case error only if a minimal complete, replayable case directory can be written: `input.json`, `output.txt`, `runner.json`, `workspace-before.json`, `workspace-after.json`, `workspace-diff.json`, and `score.json`. If enough artifacts cannot be written for deterministic `report_data`, abort as a command-level exit-3 failure. If no manifest can be written, remove the empty reservation directory so the run id is not wedged as busy forever.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two 2-second sleep cases finish in about 2 seconds with `--jobs 2` and about 4 seconds with `--jobs 1`.
- Across `--jobs 1` and `--jobs N` for deterministic runners, `report_hash`, `manifest.cases` order, per-case statuses, per-case scores, and artifact relative paths match.
- `manifest.execution.jobs`, `runner.json.duration_ms`, and other documented volatile fields may differ.
- `--jobs 0` and other values below 1 fail with `E_CASE_INVALID`.

title: Kill runner process groups
description: The runner is started in a new session, but the timeout branch only handles the direct child. Grandchildren can survive past the configured timeout, violating the execution contract.
design: Replace `subprocess.run(...)` in `run_case` with explicit `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` and `communicate(timeout=...)`. On `TimeoutExpired`, call `os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL)` with `ProcessLookupError` handling, then call `proc.communicate()` to drain and reap. Preserve existing capture behavior, task stdin handling, shell/argv behavior, partial stdout/stderr capture, normal negative-returncode signal reporting, and redaction.
acceptance_criteria:
- A runner that forks a long-lived grandchild and then blocks past `timeout_seconds` leaves no surviving grandchild.
- Timeout case artifacts show `status:"error"`, `runner.json.timed_out:true`, and `runner.json.error_code:"E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT"`.
- The run emits `W_PARTIAL_RUN`, does not emit an envelope error, exits 0 by default, and exits 6 under `--fail-on-fail`.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Replaced subprocess.run runner execution with explicit subprocess.Popen plus communicate(timeout=...).
- On timeout, kills the runner process group with os.killpg(os.getpgid(proc.pid), signal.SIGKILL), handles ProcessLookupError, then drains/reaps with communicate().
- Preserved shell/argv behavior, task stdin handling, stdout/stderr capture, timeout artifact status, and redaction flow.
- Added a regression test where the runner spawns a child which spawns a delayed marker writer; after timeout the marker is never written.
- Verified with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Enforce run-id semantic identity
description: Reusing a completed `--run-id` against a different suite or case set currently returns the stale completed run. Agents need completed-run reuse to be idempotent only when the current suite identity matches the stored manifest.
design:
On completed run-id reuse, compare the current suite name, suite hash, and sorted list of `(case_id, input_hash)` pairs against the stored manifest. A match returns the existing run with `existing:true`. A mismatch raises `E_RUN_CONFLICT` with exit 5, names the existing run-id clash, and suggests using a fresh run id. Manifest-less reservation directories remain `E_RUN_BUSY`.

Enrich the idempotent response with `run_id`, `run_dir`, `run{ok,case_count,status_counts}`, `report_hash`, and `existing:true`, using `report_data(run_dir)` where possible. Preserve `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` on this early-return path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rerunning the same suite and same run id returns exit 0, `existing:true`, `run_id`, `run_dir`, `run`, `report_hash`, and `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER`.
- Editing a case body and reusing the same run id returns `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5, and does not overwrite artifacts.
- Renaming a case id with identical content also returns `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5, and does not overwrite artifacts.
- A manifest-less reservation directory still returns `E_RUN_BUSY`, exit 4.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added current/stored run identity comparison using suite name, suite hash, and sorted (case_id, input_hash) pairs.
- Completed-run reuse now returns existing:true with run_id, run_dir, run summary, report_hash, and W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER.
- Reuse with edited case content or renamed case id now raises E_RUN_CONFLICT exit 5 without overwriting artifacts.
- Manifest-less reservation directories still return E_RUN_BUSY exit 4.
- Verified with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

title: Cap output file bytes
description: `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE` is read without a cap and `runner.json.output_truncated` is always false. This can produce unbounded artifacts and dishonest metadata.
design: Read at most `max_output_bytes` raw bytes from `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, then decode with UTF-8 replacement, mirroring stdout/stderr handling. Set `runner.json.output_truncated` truthfully and include output-file truncation in `W_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`. Truncate before redaction and before writing back to `output.txt` so the persisted artifact and scored text match. Keep scorers text-based on the decoded replacement text; byte-exact scoring is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- A runner that writes an ASCII output file larger than `max_output_bytes` produces `runner.json.output_truncated:true`.
- The run emits `W_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`.
- The captured raw bytes are capped at `max_output_bytes`; the persisted decoded file may differ in on-disk byte length for invalid or multibyte input.
- Scoring and report replay use the capped persisted artifact.

title: Skip non-UTF-8 paths
description: Workspace paths containing surrogate-escaped non-UTF-8 bytes can survive the manifest walk and later crash JSON serialization. The manifest contract should skip unreadable or unrepresentable paths with a warning rather than crashing the run.
design: In manifest path normalization, detect relative paths that cannot round-trip through strict UTF-8. Explicitly reject surrogate code points before any `stable_json(..., ensure_ascii=False)` serialization. Skip such entries and emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` with a best-effort lossy path. Preserve existing symlink, FIFO, and hash-error handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- A POSIX-only, gracefully skipped test creates a bad-byte fixture through raw bytes where the platform/filesystem allows it.
- The manifest omits the non-UTF-8 path.
- The run emits `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` naming the problematic path.
- The run still completes and scores other paths.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Changed manifest traversal sorting to use filesystem bytes so a bad relative path cannot crash before the per-path try block.
- normalize_rel now rejects paths that cannot encode as strict UTF-8, including surrogateescaped byte names.
- W_PATH_UNREADABLE messages use lossy-safe display names so warnings remain JSON-serializable.
- Added a POSIX-only/skippable raw-byte fixture test that asserts warning emission, manifest omission, and run completion where the filesystem permits the fixture.

title: Ship real schema output
description: `schema <verb>` currently returns generic object schemas with empty definitions. That creates false confidence for agents relying on the advertised machine contract.
design:
Keep the existing envelope schema and add a real module-level schema map for each implemented verb's `data` payload: `capabilities`, `schema`, `init`, `validate`, `run`, `status`, and `report`. Each schema should declare `type`, `properties`, and `required`. Top-level `data` payload schemas remain open with `additionalProperties:true` so additive fields under `contract_version:1` do not break strict validators. Close only fixed leaf structures explicitly intended never to grow.

Include current fields such as the `surface` discriminator in capabilities error codes and `existing` on the idempotent `run` response. Real schemas may change the `schema` and `capabilities` golden hashes; re-pin them intentionally.
acceptance_criteria:
- `schema run --json` returns a non-trivial `data.schemas.run` with `properties`, `required`, and top-level `additionalProperties:true`.
- All implemented verbs have genuine `data` payload schemas.
- Schema definitions are single-sourced and testable.
- The `schema` golden hash is re-pinned.
- The `capabilities` golden hash is re-pinned if its payload changed.
